'''''Anchusa azurea''''' is a [[species]] of flowering plant in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Boraginaceae, known by the common names '''garden anchusa'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> and '''Italian bugloss''' (or just "bugloss"). This bristly [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] may reach {{cvt|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall and {{cvt|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anchusa azurea 'Loddon Royalist'|url=https://www.gardenersworld.com/plants/anchusa-azurea-loddon-royalist/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=BBC Gardeners' World Magazine|language=en}}</ref> It has straight lance-shaped leaves and petite tubular flowers about 15 millimeters across with five bright violet-blue petals.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Buy Anchusa azurea Loddon Royalist AGM {{!}} Perennials|url=https://www.burford.co.uk/garden/plants/summer-garden/anchusa-azurea-loddon-royalist/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Burford Garden Company|language=en}}</ref> These flowers, which typically appear in May–July, are edible and attract bees.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anchusa azurea Loddon Royalist'|url=https://www.sarahraven.com/flowers/plants/perennials-spring-summer-planting/anchusa-azurea-loddon-royalist.htm|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Sarah Raven|language=en}}</ref> This species is [[native plant|native]] to Europe, western Asia, and eastern [[Maghreb]].<ref>[http://ww2.bgbm.org/EuroPlusMed/query.asp The Euro+Med PlantBase - the information resource for Euro-Mediterranean plant diversity].[http://euromed.luomus.fi/euromed_map.php?taxon=435542&size=medium Details for:Anchusa azurea]. Accessed on 10 March 2012.</ref>

The genus name ''[[Anchusa]]'' comes from the [[Greek language|Greek]] 'ankousa', which is the name of a root pigment once used for cosmetic purposes.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-03-27|title=How to Grow Anchusa (Anchusa Azurea, Dropmore Flower, Italian Bugloss)|url=https://www.gardeningchannel.com/how-to-grow-anchusa-flowers/|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Gardening Channel|language=en-US}}</ref>

Numerous [[cultivar]]s have been developed for garden use, including 'Dropmore', 'Feltham Pride', 'Little John', 'Loddon Royalist' and 'Opal'.<ref name=":0" />

In the [[United States|US]] it is suitable for [[hardiness zone]]s 3–8. It grows best in full sun with good drainage, and is [[Drought tolerance|drought tolerant]] once established.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Anchusa azurea (Italian Bugloss)|url=https://www.gardenia.net/plant/anchusa-azurea-italian-bugloss|access-date=2021-04-28|website=Gardenia.net}}</ref> It may be susceptible to [[Leaf miner|leafminer]] and [[powdery mildew]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Anchusa (Bugloss)|url=https://www.seasonalgardening.co.uk/perennials/anchusa.asp|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.seasonalgardening.co.uk|language=en}}</ref>
